Theme 055 · Signature directions

Bento Grid

Every frame is a 6×6 bento of white tiles — the feature-summary language of keynote slides and modern SaaS landing pages. One fixed shell (r16 · gap 16 · pad 28), one message and one micro-motion per tile; the seams between scenes are either diving into a tile or collapsing the whole grid into one.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Shell — 6×6 grid, radius 16, gutter 16, inner padding 28 — never changes between scenes
  • Anchor tile — the frame’s single message, 2–4× the area of its neighbours
  • Giant number tile — one mono numeral 80–130 px that counts in
  • Ink table tile — the only dark tile: your data, crossed by a teal scan band
  • Anomaly tile — coral inset border + coral −18%; slams in and nudges its neighbours
  • Tile-zoom seam — dive into a tile to start the next scene, or collapse the grid into one hero tile

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Tile cascade — scale .92 → 1 + opacity, power2.out 0.4 s, 70 ms stagger large→small; big tiles on beats, small on off-beats
  • Micro-motion per tile — each tile owns one loop (count, sparkline draw, badge blink) lasting exactly 1 bar = 2 s at 120 BPM
  • Grid collapse — all tiles translate to centre + merge radii over 0.5 s expo.in, landing precisely on the drop

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

Bento is the most scannable way to show many capabilities at once, and a muted feed can read each tile as a separate caption. Risk: equal-weight tiles become a busy dashboard — insist on one anchor per frame and let empty tiles breathe.

Adapt to your product: Map each tile to one fact about your product (a metric, an integration, a screenshot crop) and keep a single “hero” tile per frame; the collapse/zoom seams work for any feature list.

References: https://www.saasframe.io/blog/the-bento-layout-trend (why the bento layout took over SaaS pages) · https://saaspo.com/style/bento (gallery of bento SaaS landing pages)
